why: Puts fire back on button 0, A/Cross. That is under the same right thumb that has to hold the aim stick, so a twin-stick player can aim or fire but not both -- the ergonomic defect this binding was moved to fix. It also re-collides with MENU_CONFIRM_BUTTON, restoring the leaked-shell class issue #494 was filed for: confirming Resume with A, still held on the first simulated tick, reads as a fresh fire press. TWO tests catch it and they catch different halves, which is why both are named: one pins the index as the trigger, the other pins menu and gameplay buttons as disjoint sets. The behavioural edge tests deliberately do NOT catch it -- they press through the constant, so they measure edge semantics rather than binding, and a binding change should not disturb them.
